observation.visible_scene: A blue hydraulic shop press stands on a workbench. Inside its frame, a red hydraulic bottle jack with a looped carrying handle rests on the base plate, its horizontal handle bar sitting just below the press's silver ram. On the right is the press's blue pump cylinder with a white-gripped lever. The background shows green cabinets and a wall with cables and a red switch; two white warning labels are fixed to the top crossbeam.
visible_changes: A hand repeatedly grips the white pump lever and works it through a vertical pumping stroke, cycling between a low, near-horizontal position (e.g. frames 7-10, 17-19, 26-28, 35-37) and a raised, angled-up position (e.g. frames 4-5, 13-14, 22-23, 31-32, 40-41), at a rate of roughly one stroke per ~0.6 s.

The press ram, the red jack, the blue frame and the labels keep constant positions relative to each other and to the background across the excerpt; no clearly measurable descent of the ram onto the jack is visible.
The camera is stationary: background cabinets, wall cables and labels do not shift, so all observed motion is object motion (the lever/hand), not camera motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether continued pumping eventually lowers the ram or deforms the jack, and what the intended test or operation is.
Whether the ram was already in contact with the jack's handle bar before the excerpt began.
uncertain_details: Any ram movement is too small to confirm against the static reference points.
The exact contact point between the ram and the red jack is not clearly resolved.
The operator's body and the purpose of the setup are outside the frame.
